LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 7.3.1 RELATIVE PRONOUNS: INTERROGATIVE PRONOUNS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Relative Pronouns: Interrogative Pronouns

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Relative Pronouns: Interrogative Pronouns. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you obtain information from people?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognise relative and interrogative pronouns in a text
2. use relative and interrogative pronouns in sentences

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: GRAMMAR IN USE 7.3.1 RELATIVE PRONOUNS: INTERROGATIVE PRONOUNS
This lesson teaches Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Relative Pronouns: Interrogative Pronouns for Grade 9 ENGLISH.

STUDY STEPS
1. recognise relative and interrogative pronouns in a text
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. use relative and interrogative pronouns in sentences
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Relative Pronouns: Interrogative Pronouns using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Relative Pronouns: Interrogative Pronouns above.
2. Explain Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Relative Pronouns: Interrogative Pronouns to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Relative Pronouns: Interrogative Pronouns.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Relative Pronouns: Interrogative Pronouns with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Relative Pronouns: Interrogative Pronouns important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you obtain information from people?
2. Which words do you use to ask questions and to join simple sentences?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. recognise relative and interrogative pronouns in a text
2. use relative and interrogative pronouns in sentences

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
